article_title: Implementation and Outcomes of Kansas Multi-Tier System of Supports: Final Evaluation Report-2014
citation: Kristin Reedy, Ed.D., and Natalie Lacireno-Paquet, Ph.D. (2015). Implementation and Outcomes of Kansas Multi-Tier System of Supports: Final Evaluation Report—2014. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: KSDE statewide MTSS support infrastructure (Core Team, Recognized Facilitators, Symposium, website, dissemination)
description: The Kansas State Department of Education maintains a statewide infrastructure to support and sustain MTSS implementation. Its components "include the MTSS Core Team, the cadre of Recognized MTSS Facilitators, the annual MTSS Symposium, an extensive and frequently updated website of materials, research, and resources on MTSS, and an ongoing dissemination plan" coordinated with the Technical Assistance System Network. In the 2014 survey, 77.4% of respondents reported KSDE established the necessary infrastructure to sustain and extend MTSS, 75.9% reported effective dissemination, and 76.0% reported sufficient resources.
requirements: Sustained leadership and support from KSDE, including the Office of the Commissioner, and investment in district-level capacity building and strengthening of the Core Team
constraints: Sixty-one percent of respondents agreed there are sufficient MTSS Facilitators to support MTSS statewide, indicating a perceived facilitator supply limit
target_learners: Kansas public schools and districts implementing MTSS
target_learning_goals: statewide implementation of MTSS with fidelity and sustainability over time
examples: Professional development materials are aligned with the Learning Forward standards (2012), and the annual Kansas MTSS Symposium was observed by evaluators each year
key_sources: Kristin Reedy, Ed.D., and Natalie Lacireno-Paquet, Ph.D. (2015). Implementation and Outcomes of Kansas Multi-Tier System of Supports: Final Evaluation Report—2014. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED559729

article_title: OpenLearnLM Benchmark: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Knowledge, Skill, and Attitude in Educational Large Language Models
citation: Unggi Lee, Sookbun Lee, Heungsoo Choi, Jinseo Lee, Haeun Park, Younghoon Jeon, Sungmin Cho, Minju Kang, Junbo Koh, Jiyeong Bae, Minwoo Nam, Juyeon Eun, Yeonji Jung, Yeil Jeong. (2026). OpenLearnLM Benchmark: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Knowledge, Skill, and Attitude in Educational Large Language Models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13882
title: KSA three-axis evaluation framework with a four-level Skills hierarchy (Center→Role→Scenario→Sub-scenario)
description: The framework operationalizes educational LLM capability using the KSA (Knowledge-Skills-Attitude) model from educational assessment. The article states: "The Skills domain comprises 122,425 items across 6 Centers, 11 Roles, 46 Scenarios, and 81 Sub-scenarios." Knowledge covers curriculum-based content and pedagogical knowledge; Skills measures situated capability through tasks emulating real educational decisions, with difficulty tiers from Bloom's and Krathwohl's taxonomies; Attitude examines epistemic, instructional, and normative-ethical stances plus deception resistance via Alignment Faking. The hierarchy contextualizes tasks by institutional function (Center), professional responsibility (Role), task type (Scenario), and task variant (Sub-scenario).
requirements: Evaluation requires domain-matched methods: exact-match accuracy for Knowledge, LLM-as-Judge with scenario-specific 10-point rubrics for Skills, and LLM-as-Judge plus Alignment Faking comparison for Attitude
constraints: The framework is grounded in the KSA model from educational assessment and Bloom's/Krathwohl's taxonomies; the article notes future work is needed for multilingual contexts and real classroom interaction data
target_learners: LLMs acting as educational partners across teaching, learning, assessment, counseling, research, and administration contexts
target_learning_goals: Multidimensional educational competence beyond factual accuracy, including situated skill and pedagogical value alignment
examples: Each of the 81 sub-scenarios has a dedicated 10-point rubric defining quality levels from inadequate (1–2) to exemplary (9–10)

OpenLearnLM Benchmark: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Knowledge, Skill, and Attitude in Educational Large Language Models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13882

article_title: Synthesizing frameworks of higher education student learning outcomes
citation: Markle, R., Brenneman, M., Jackson, T., Burrus, J., & Robbins, S. (2013). Synthesizing Frameworks of Higher Education Student Learning Outcomes. ETS Research Report Series, ETS RR-13-22. http://search.ets.org/researcher
title: KSAVE framework of 21st century skills
description: The KSAVE framework, produced in Phase 1 of the ATC21S project sponsored by Cisco, Intel, and Microsoft and led by the University of Melbourne, organizes skills for success in the 21st century by knowledge, skills, attitudes, values, and ethics. "The KSAVE framework uses 10 skills, grouped into four categories": ways of thinking, ways of working, tools for working, and living in the world. For each skill it provides knowledge requirements, guiding abilities and skills, and related behaviors and aptitudes.
requirements: Provides reference to knowledge requirements, abilities and skills that guide curriculum, and behaviors and aptitudes related to each skill
constraints: Developed to guide creation of large-scale assessments of 21st century skills rather than specifically for bachelor's-level higher education outcomes
target_learners: students being prepared for the 21st century workforce
examples: ATC21S was initiated by Cisco, Intel, and Microsoft in cooperation with the University of Melbourne and the countries of Australia, Finland, Singapore, and the United States

article_title: Formation of the Professional and Didactic Culture of the Future Teacher
citation: Mirzagitova, A. L. & Akhmetov, L. G. (2016). Formation of the Professional and Didactic Culture of the Future Teacher. International Journal of Environmental & Science Education, 11(14), 6675-6689. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1118411
title: Ksenzova matrix of ways of organizing pupils' activities in authoritarian and humanistic teaching paradigms
description: The article uses a matrix elaborated by G.Y. Ksenzova (2004) determining the ways of organizing pupils' activities in the authoritarian and humanistic teaching paradigms. It contrasts the two paradigms across five activity components: purpose, motives, means, actions, result and assessment. Students used this matrix during teaching practice to determine the teaching paradigm of their teachers.
requirements: Students were provided with the matrix as part of the determination of the teaching paradigm during teaching practice.
examples: In the humanistic paradigm, self-assessment on the basis of application of the individual achievement standards replaces comparison with generally accepted standards.
key_sources: Mirzagitova, A. L. & Akhmetov, L. G. (2016). Formation of the Professional and Didactic Culture of the Future Teacher. International Journal of Environmental & Science Education, 11(14), 6675-6689. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1115889

article_title: Exploring core competence in first-year medical students through narrative medicine and peer-assisted learning: a mixed-methods study.
citation: Lin Peixin, Yin Xiaolin, Zheng Xuankun, He Sijia, Cai Yuexin, Deng Xiaozheng, Chen Tongtong, Liang Weiquan, Liang Suqiong, Liang Yuanke, Lu Yiwen, Lin Haoyu. (2026). Exploring core competence in first-year medical students through narrative medicine and peer-assisted learning: a mixed-methods study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10160-7
title: A 19-indicator Delphi-developed Knowledge-Skills-Attitude (KSA) self-report scale for first-year medical students' core competence
description: The article developed a 19-item KSA scale to operationalize core competence across Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes dimensions, with indicators extracted via scoping review and refined through two rounds of Delphi consultation with 18 experts (authority coefficient 0.74). In the study sample it showed acceptable internal consistency (α = 0.878) and preliminary construct validity (KMO = 0.843), with exploratory factor analysis supporting a three-factor structure consistent with the KSA framework. The authors caution it is "a preliminary instrument with emerging validity evidence" requiring validation in larger, independent samples.
requirements: Two rounds of Delphi expert consultation to establish indicator consensus
Further validation in larger, independent samples
constraints: Developed and initially validated using the same sample later used to evaluate the intervention
Knowledge subscale reliability was modest (α = 0.625, four items)
target_learning_goals: Self-assessment of early-stage core competence across knowledge, skills, and attitudes
key_sources: Lin Peixin, Yin Xiaolin, Zheng Xuankun, He Sijia, Cai Yuexin, Deng Xiaozheng, Chen Tongtong, Liang Weiquan, Liang Suqiong, Liang Yuanke, Lu Yiwen, Lin Haoyu. (2026). article_title: Medical students' perspectives on the role of OSPE and OSCE in the educational journey and contribution to career development: A cross-sectional study.
citation: Alrashed FA, Ahmad T, Alsubiheen AM, Alhammad SA, Aldaihan MM, Albishi AM, Hasan Z. (2026). Medical students’ perspectives on the role of OSPE and OSCE in the educational journey and contribution to career development: A cross-sectional study. Medicine 2026;105:3(e47233). https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000047233
title: Blueprint-based OSCE/OSPE assessment system at King Saud University College of Medicine
description: A structured practical and clinical assessment system in which "OSCE and OSPE exams are conducted based on the Course Learning Outcomes of each course or block." Each assessment item is mapped to course learning outcomes and a blueprint is created using a checklist prepared according to Bloom's taxonomy, with items and stations validated by the exam committee and senior faculty before final student assessments. The College of Medicine runs 12 stations per track, each of 3-minute duration, with OSCE timing of 6 to 10 minutes depending on the case.
requirements: Assessment items must be mapped to Course Learning Outcomes with a blueprint checklist prepared according to Bloom's taxonomy.
Validation of all assessment items and stations by the exam committee along with 2 or 3 senior faculty members before final student assessments.
constraints: The system is described as implemented at the College of Medicine, King Saud University, within a 3-phase MBBS curriculum; station format is fixed at 12 stations per track with 3-minute stations and 6–10 minute OSCE timing.
target_learners: 1st to 5th-year medical students in a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery program
target_learning_goals: Clinical competence including history-taking, clinical examination, communication, decision-making, and professionalism
Practical and technical skills such as handling instruments, conducting experiments, or performing procedures
examples: A pilot study of the accompanying questionnaire was conducted on May 11, 2024, with 33 participants, yielding a Cronbach alpha of 0.794.

article_title: Performance of ChatGPT in the In-Training Examination for Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine Residents in South Korea: Observational Study.
citation: Lesselroth Blake; Bruthans Jan; Hidki Asmaa; Yoon Soo-Hyuk; Oh Seok Kyeong; Lim Byung Gun; Lee Ho-Jin. (2024). Performance of ChatGPT in the In-Training Examination for Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine Residents in South Korea: Observational Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/56859
title: Korean Society of Anesthesiologists in-training examination question set (398 text-only questions, 2018-2022)
description: A curated evaluation corpus of 398 multiple-choice questions drawn from the KSA in-training examinations administered to Korean anesthesiology residents from 2018 to 2022, each year comprising 100 questions. Questions "containing images, diagrams, or photographs were excluded from the analysis" because ChatGPT accepts only text input. Each question has one query and five choices with one correct answer, and the set spans 21 subfields of anesthesiology and pain medicine.
requirements: Access to KSA member-only question texts, answer keys, and commentaries via the official website
constraints: Excludes image-based questions, limiting representativeness of full examinations
Direct comparison with resident scores was not possible due to the exclusions
target_learning_goals: assessment of medical knowledge and reasoning in anesthesiology
examples: Used to compare GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and CLOVA X under identical Korean-language prompting conditions
key_sources: Lesselroth Blake; Bruthans Jan; Hidki Asmaa; Yoon Soo-Hyuk; Oh Seok Kyeong; Lim Byung Gun; Lee Ho-Jin. (2024). Performance of ChatGPT in the In-Training Examination for Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine Residents in South Korea: Observational Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/56859
